text: TAREEQ answers questions about Dubai Roads and Transport legislation.
Choose how to search: hybrid, keywords or meaning. Filter by year and document type.
Pick an example question, or type your own.
A loading card shows while the assistant searches, ranks and writes.
Every answer has numbered sources, and each sentence is checked against the document.
Click [1] to open that source: the document, the page, and the sentences that rely on it.
A button opens the official page. Not legal advice: always check the source.
Follow-up questions work: the conversation is remembered.
"It" is understood from the earlier question.
A vague question: start a new conversation and ask "What is the fine?"
The assistant pauses and asks. The answer box is right inside the card.
Typing the answer resumes the paused question.
Same conversation, now answered with sources.
Outside the topic? It refuses politely and invents no answer.
Not covered by the documents? It says so instead of guessing.
Past conversations are saved in this browser. Open one to continue it.
Delete one: a toast offers Undo.
The Search Inspector shows what the search finds, before any answer is written.
Each passage shows its rank, page, a labelled score, and its position before reranking.
Lexical mode uses keyword scores (BM25): a different scale, never compared with the others.
A filter that matches no document returns an empty result.
The About page explains how it works and states its limits.
